effects: Takes exactly `assets` USDC from the signer into the vault (SafeERC20Lib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets) in enter), using the signer's USDC allowance to the vault.
Mints previewDeposit(assets) gtUSDCp shares to `onBehalf`. The share count comes from the vault's stored totals after fees accrue, and there is no minimum-shares parameter.
Accrues interest first, which can mint fee shares to the fee recipients and so lower the share price the signer gets.
formats.shown: Deposit 1 USDC for <onBehalf>, with fields for the USDC amount, the share ticker 'gtusdcp' and the share recipient. The number of shares is not shown.

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares received is not shown; the code derives it from storage and has no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);` uses accrueInterestView() storage totals. Case 0: the signer received 1e18 gtUSDCp, but the screen shows only 'Share ticker: gtusdcp' and gives no amount.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds the shares. Keep the ticker field; a fix would need a slippage-protected entry point (for example a router with minShares).

findings.title: deposit: the vaultTicker constant 'gtusdcp' differs in case from the on-chain symbol 'gtUSDCp'.
findings.evidence: descriptor metadata.constants.vaultTicker = "gtusdcp". Case 0 mined effect symbol for 0x8c106eed… is "gtUSDCp".

cases.notes: The 1 USDC out is shown correctly. The 1 gtUSDCp in has its asset and recipient shown but no amount, and the code provides no bound, so the reader could not know the share count.

effects: Takes previewMint(shares) USDC (rounded up) from the signer into the vault. The amount comes from the vault's stored totals, and there is no maximum-assets parameter.
Accrues interest first, which can mint fee shares to the fee recipients.
formats.shown: Mint <shares> gtusdcp for <onBehalf>, with a field that names USDC as the deposit asset but gives no USDC amount.

findings.title: mint: the intent and the sentence never say that USDC leaves the signer's wallet.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint intent "Mint", interpolatedIntent "Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}". VaultV2.sol enter: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)`. Case 1: the signer paid 1 unit of USDC, and the sentence reads 'Mint 0.000000001 gtusdcp for 0x…dEaD'.
findings.fix: Use intent "Deposit USDC for shares" and interpolatedIntent "Deposit USDC to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}".

findings.title: mint: the USDC amount paid is not shown; the code derives it from storage and has no maximum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares);` (mulDivUp on stored totals). Case 1: 1 USDC base unit left the signer, and the screen shows 'Deposit asset: USDC' with no amount.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds the assets. Label the field 'Pay with (amount set by vault price)'.

cases.notes: The only signer effect is USDC out. The screen names USDC but not the amount. The reader correctly saw that the shares go to 0xdead.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns previewWithdraw(assets) gtUSDCp (rounded up) from `onBehalf`. The amount comes from storage, and there is no maximum-shares parameter.
When msg.sender != onBehalf, spends the caller's share allowance from onBehalf by the burned shares.
Sends exactly `assets` USDC from the vault to `receiver`.
Accrues interest first, which can mint fee shares to the fee recipients.
formats.shown: Withdraw <assets> USDC to <receiver>, with fields for the exact USDC amount, the receiver and the owner. The shares burned are not shown.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of gtUSDCp shares burned is not shown; the code derives it from storage.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);` then deleteShares(onBehalf, shares). Case 2: the signer burned 988044.156… gtUSDCp, and no field states shares.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds the shares. Change the 'Owner' label to 'Shares burned from'.

cases.notes: The 1,000,000 USDC in is shown correctly with its receiver. The shares out are implied by 'Owner' but have no amount; the reader guessed shares are burned.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns exactly `shares` gtUSDCp from `onBehalf`, spending the caller's share allowance when msg.sender != onBehalf.
Sends previewRedeem(shares) USDC from the vault to `receiver`. The amount comes from storage, and there is no minimum-assets parameter.
Accrues interest first, which can mint fee shares to the fee recipients.
formats.shown: Redeem <shares> gtusdcp to <receiver>, with fields for shares, receiver and owner. Nothing says that USDC is received, nor how much.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never names USDC as the asset received, though a constant field could.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` with asset = USDC. Descriptor redeem fields: shares, receiver, onBehalf only. Case 3: the signer received 40000.230963 USDC, and the reader wrote 'Which token is paid out; I assume USDC'.
findings.fix: Add a field {"label":"Receive asset","format":"raw","value":"$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"} and set interpolatedIntent to "Redeem {#.shares} for USDC to {#.receiver}".

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount received is not shown; the code derives it from storage and has no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. Case 3: 40000230963 USDC units arrived, and no field shows an amount or bound.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds the assets. Only a slippage-protected entry point could bound it.

cases.notes: The shares out are shown exactly. For the USDC in, the asset is only guessed and the amount is absent.
